key_insight: By combining phase-amplitude reduction with sparse-sensor machine learning, the study computes optimal actuation waveforms that rapidly retune airfoil wake shedding while constraining lift fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical control strategy for post-stall airfoils and other periodic aeroelastic systems where fast flow modification must be achieved without inducing large aerodynamic oscillations.
method: Use only three sparse sensors to reconstruct wake state and estimate phase/amplitude sensitivity fields.
Derive optimal time-varying forcing waveforms analytically from the sensitivity fields for fast synchronization.
Add an amplitude penalty to reduce lift-coefficient fluctuations during frequency control.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on multiple NACA airfoils at several post-stall angles of attack with periodic vortex shedding; the optimal forcing changed wake frequency faster than sinusoidal actuation and the amplitude-penalized version reduced lift fluctuations by 20%.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate sparse-sensor reconstruction and sensitivity modeling, so performance may degrade if the flow departs from the assumed periodic regime or if sensor noise is strong.
paper_title: Machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction for fast synchronization of airfoil wakes with constrained fluctuations
